extracted.intended_audience: registrants (public companies), their accountants, auditors, and counsel preparing SEC reports and registration statements
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and instructions under Item 305 of Regulation S-K for preparing quantitative and qualitative disclosures about market risk in SEC reports and registration statements, including choice of disclosure alternative, required content, model disclosures, and presentation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide quantitative information about market risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants shall provide, in their reporting currency, quantitative information about market risk as of the end of the latest fiscal year, in accordance with one of the following three disclosure alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In preparing this quantitative information, registrants shall categorize market risk sensitive instruments into instruments entered into for trading purposes and instruments entered into for purposes other than trading purposes. Within both portfolios, separate quantitative information shall be presented, to the extent material, for each market risk exposure category (i.e., interest rate risk, foreign currency exchange rate risk, commodity price risk, and other relevant market risks, such as equity price risk). A registrant may use one alternative for all disclosures, may choose different alternatives for trading vs other than trading, or may choose any alternative for each risk exposure category within the portfolios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure alternatives (three permitted methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: The three disclosure alternatives are: (i) tabular presentation of information related to market risk sensitive instruments; (ii) sensitivity analysis disclosures; and (iii) value at risk disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registrant must choose one of the three alternatives for required quantitative disclosures, but may mix alternatives across portfolios or risk categories as described in paragraph (a)(1). Each alternative has its own content and model/assumption disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabular presentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Tabular presentation must include fair values of the market risk sensitive instruments and contract terms sufficient to determine future cash flows from those instruments, categorized by expected maturity dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tabular information relating to contract terms shall allow readers to determine expected cash flows for each of the next five years; comparable tabular information for remaining years may be aggregated. See Appendix for suggested format. Registrants shall provide a description of the contents of the table and any related assumptions necessary to understand the disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabular grouping and contract-term examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Within each risk exposure category, market risk sensitive instruments shall be grouped based on common characteristics; within foreign currency exchange rate risk group by functional currency; within commodity price risk group by type of commodity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of contract terms sufficient to determine future cash flows include: debt—principal amounts and weighted average effective interest rates; forwards and futures—contract amounts and weighted average settlement prices; options—contract amounts and weighted average strike prices; swaps—notional amounts and weighted average pay/receive rates; complex instruments—combination of these terms. When grouping, at minimum consider fixed vs variable rate, long vs short forwards/futures, written vs purchased options with similar strikes, swap types, currency of cash flows, derivatives used to manage anticipated transactions, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity analysis disclosures (content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensitivity analysis disclosures must express the potential loss in future earnings, fair values, or cash flows of market risk sensitive instruments resulting from one or more selected hypothetical changes in interest rates, foreign currency exchange rates, commodity prices, and other relevant market rates or prices over a selected period of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magnitude of selected hypothetical changes may differ among and within market risk exposure categories. Registrants shall provide a description of the model, assumptions, and parameters necessary to understand the sensitivity analysis (e.g., how loss is defined, modeling technique, instruments covered, how optionality is addressed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity analysis selection rules and parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Select hypothetical changes expected to reflect reasonably possible near-term changes; absent economic justification, use changes not less than 10% of end-of-period market rates or prices. 'Reasonably possible' and 'near term' have GAAP meanings (near term = up to one year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include instruments exposed to more than one market risk category in each relevant sensitivity analysis. For multiple foreign currency exchange exposures, prepare a foreign currency sensitivity analysis that measures aggregate sensitivity to changes in all FX exposures (including transactional/functional and functional/reporting exposures). Model description should include definition of loss, general modeling technique (duration modeling, present-value change, treatment of optionality), types of instruments covered, magnitude/timing of selected hypothetical changes, method for discount rates, and prepayment/reinvestment assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value at risk (VaR) disclosures (content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Value at risk disclosures must express the potential loss in future earnings, fair values, or cash flows of market risk sensitive instruments over a selected period of time, with a selected likelihood of occurrence, from changes in relevant market rates or prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each category requiring VaR, provide either (i) the average, high and low amounts or distribution of VaR amounts for the reporting period; (ii) the average, high and low amounts or distribution of actual changes in fair values/earnings/cash flows during the reporting period; or (iii) the percentage or number of times actual changes exceeded the VaR amounts. Information required under certain VaR subparagraphs is not required for the first fiscal year the registrant must present Item 305 information. Registrants shall provide a description of the model, assumptions, and parameters necessary to understand VaR disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value at risk model and parameter guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe model type and parameters used to derive VaR and how optionality and instrument coverage are handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested model types include variance/covariance, historical simulation, or Monte Carlo simulation. Describe how optionality is addressed, types of instruments covered, holding periods, confidence intervals, and methods used for aggregating VaR across exposure categories (e.g., assume perfect positive correlation, independence, or observed correlation). Confidence intervals should reflect reasonably possible near-term changes; absent justification use intervals 95% or higher. 'Near term' and 'reasonably possible' have GAAP meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss material limitations of quantitative disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants shall discuss material limitations that cause the information required under paragraph (a)(1) not to fully reflect the net market risk exposures of the entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This discussion shall include summarized descriptions of instruments, positions, and transactions omitted from quantitative disclosures or features of included instruments that are not fully reflected (e.g., derivatives not settled in cash, commodity positions, cash flows from anticipated transactions, instruments with leverage or option/prepayment features). Failure to include such items may mean disclosures do not fully reflect net market risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present summarized prior-year market risk information
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants shall present summarized market risk information for the preceding fiscal year and discuss reasons for material quantitative changes in market risk exposures between current and preceding fiscal years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information is not required if disclosure is not required under paragraph (a)(1) for the current fiscal year, and is not required for the first fiscal year end in which a registrant must present Item 305 information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain material changes in disclosure method or models
rubrics_metrics.description: If registrants change disclosure alternatives or key model characteristics, assumptions, and parameters used in providing quantitative information about market risk and the effects are material, the registrant shall explain the reasons for the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The registrant shall either (i) provide summarized comparable information, under the new disclosure method, for the year preceding the current year; or (ii) provide disclosures for the current year and preceding fiscal year under the method used in the preceding year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality assessment for each market risk exposure category
rubrics_metrics.description: A materiality assessment should be made for each market risk exposure category within the trading and other than trading portfolios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants should evaluate both (i) the materiality of the fair values of derivative financial instruments, other financial instruments, and derivative commodity instruments outstanding as of the end of the latest fiscal year; and (ii) the materiality of potential near-term losses in future earnings, fair values, and/or cash flows from reasonably possible near-term changes in market rates or prices. If either is material, the registrant should disclose quantitative and qualitative information for that category. For materiality, consider past market movements, reasonably possible near-term movements, and potential losses from leverage, option, and multiplier features. Generally do not net fair values except as allowed under GAAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorize market risk sensitive instruments into trading and other-than-trading
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants shall categorize market risk sensitive instruments into instruments entered into for trading purposes and instruments entered into for purposes other than trading purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present separate quantitative and qualitative information, as appropriate, for trading and other-than-trading portfolios. 'Trading purposes' means dealing and other trading activities measured at fair value with gains and losses recognized in earnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and scope of market risk sensitive instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: For Item 305, 'market risk sensitive instruments' include derivative financial instruments, other financial instruments, and derivative commodity instruments as defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derivative financial instruments have GAAP meanings (futures, forwards, swaps, options, etc.). 'Other financial instruments' means financial instruments for which fair value disclosures are required (examples: trade receivables, investments, loans, structured notes, mortgage-backed securities, indexed debt, interest-only/principal-only obligations, deposits, other debt obligations), and excludes items such as pension obligations, insurance contracts, lease contracts, warranty obligations, investments accounted for under equity method, noncontrolling interests, and equity instruments classified in stockholders' equity. 'Derivative commodity instruments' include commodity futures, forwards, swaps, options, and similar instruments permitted by contract/business custom to be settled in cash or with another financial instrument (cash settlement includes net cash settlement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary inclusion of other instruments and comprehensive presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants are encouraged, but not required, to include other market risk sensitive instruments/positions/transactions within the Item 305 disclosures; if included voluntarily they may present comprehensive disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants that voluntarily include other instruments within sensitivity analysis or VaR disclosures are not required to provide separate market risk disclosures for those voluntarily selected instruments. Registrants that choose the tabular alternative should present voluntarily selected instruments consistent with Item 305(a) requirements. If electing to include a particular type voluntarily, include all, rather than some, of those instruments (e.g., entire commodity position).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation location and cross-referencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Present Item 305 information outside of, and not incorporate into, the financial statements (including footnotes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants are encouraged to provide required information in one location. Alternative presentation (e.g., Management's Discussion and Analysis) may be used at registrant's discretion. If disclosed in more than one location, provide cross-references to related disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative market risk disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent material, describe the registrant's primary market risk exposures; how those exposures are managed (including objectives, general strategies, and instruments used); and changes in exposures or how they are managed compared to the most recently completed fiscal year and what is known or expected to be in effect in future reporting periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualitative information shall be presented separately for market risk sensitive instruments entered into for trading purposes and those entered into for purposes other than trading. 'Primary market risk exposures' means the categories of market risk and, within each, the particular markets that present the primary risk (e.g., dollar/yen, dollar/pound). Describe exposures as of the end of the latest fiscal year and how they are managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim period discussion requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If interim period financial statements are included or required, discussion and analysis shall be provided so as to enable the reader to assess the sources and effects of material changes in information that would be provided under Item 305 from the end of the preceding fiscal year to the date of the most recent interim balance sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures interim disclosures explain material movement in market risk exposures and management actions during the interim period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Averaging periods for sensitivity analysis or VaR
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants may report average, high, and low sensitivity analysis or VaR amounts for the reporting period as an alternative to reporting year-end amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When determining the average, registrants should use sensitivity analysis or VaR amounts relating to at least four equal time periods throughout the reporting period (e.g., four quarter-end amounts, 12 month-end amounts, or 52 week-end amounts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation and grouping guidance for currencies and multi-exposure instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants may aggregate information regarding functional currencies that are economically related, managed together for internal risk management, and have statistical correlations greater than 75% over each of the past three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Market risk sensitive instruments exposed to rate or price changes in more than one market risk exposure category should be presented in the tabular information for each risk category to which they are exposed. If a currency swap eliminates all foreign currency exposures in the cash flows of a foreign currency denominated debt instrument, neither the swap nor the debt instrument are required to be disclosed in the foreign currency risk exposure category; however, both should be disclosed in the interest rate risk exposure category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on first-year requirements and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain Item 305 sub-requirements (e.g., particular VaR detail) are not required for the first fiscal year end in which a registrant must present Item 305 information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also, disclosures called for by paragraph (a) need not be provided if previously reported as defined in Rule 12b-2, except that paragraph (a) must be provided notwithstanding prior disclosure if required pursuant to Item 9 of Schedule 14A. Paragraph (b) disclosures must be furnished notwithstanding any prior disclosure about accountant changes or disagreements.
